question.problem:
Negate the following statement:

$\,$ For all $q\in Z,$ ${q}^{2}$ is even.
question.worked_solution:
If we denote

$$
P(q):{q}^{2}\text{ is even},
$$

our statement can be written as

$$
∀q\in Z,\,P(q).
$$

Negating this, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}¬(∀q\in Z,\,P(q)) & ≡∃q\in Z,\,\text{ }¬P(q).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, $∃q\in Z,\,¬P(q)$ reads as follows:

$\,$ **There exists** $q\in Z$ such that ${q}^{2}$ is **not** even.
